By the way, I noticed that PR #9164  addressed the first issue, but I believe that the fix in my PR is superior. 

PR #9164  detects whether the window is an IME window during message processing and skips it. In my approach, I use a Vec to keep track of windows created by Zed for polling. 

I believe my solution is better because: Currently, I estimate that less than 1% of Zed users use IME, and among these users, like myself, I only use IME approximately 1% of the time while programming. Given such low usage frequency, I think it's somewhat wasteful in terms of CPU time to check for IME status 60 times per second. Therefore, I opted for the method in this PR.

> According to Windows recommendations, character input should be obtained using WM_CHAR instead of WM_KEYDOWN. Additionally, there are problems with the handling within WM_CHAR.

Yes that's true, however for keys like `ctrl-a`, control characters are generated so by capturing them in the `WM_KEYDOWN` event you avoid having to check for control characters and extra translated messages. For that reason I opted to handle those such character in `WM_KEYDOWN` instead. If checking for the control characters helps with proper IME support then fair enough, however.

> > According to Windows recommendations, character input should be obtained using WM_CHAR instead of WM_KEYDOWN. Additionally, there are problems with the handling within WM_CHAR.
>

For that reason I opted to handle those such character in `WM_KEYDOWN` instead. If checking for the control characters helps with proper IME support then fair enough, however.

In this PR, controls like `ctrl-a` are handled within `WM_KEYDOWN` event, all char events are handled within `WM_CHAR`, so that microsoft will translate and dispath for us. 
- "microsoft will translate for us" so we dont have to care about the corner case involving unicode chars.
- "microsoft will dispath for us" so we dont have to check if we are handling IME window events or not, which will cause a crash

> In this PR, controls like ctrl-a are handled within WM_KEYDOWN event

> I understand where it's being handled in WM_KEYDOWN. I was pointing out that it was being translated/dispatched regardless for the new code. Are you saying that translating a ctrl-a keydown event is required for IME? If so then great and I understand the reason for change.

Sometimes, even though the timer is set to trigger every 16ms, in some heavy scenarios, it might take 100ms for the timer to trigger, possibly due to scheduling and thread priority. So, scheduling a redraw here to prompt Zed to react as soon as possible.

with `DCompositionWaitForCompositorClock` being used invalidating the rect won't trigger another message. I understand with the timer it's beneficial, but forcing an invalidate on input is more like a hack than a fix.
